confirmed.claim: Our description body is the legacy Secrets of Magic text (feat-2848: a one-action 'Requirements You're holding a book' action that stays raised until your next turn) on a remaster record whose aonId feat-9046 prints a passive feat that modifies Raise a Shield and adds a reinforcing-rune inscription; the reinforcing-rune mechanic is missing from both the description and the note.
confirmed.printed: When you Raise a Shield, you can raise a book you’re wielding instead of a shield. While you have a book raised, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and a +1 circumstance bonus to Recall Knowledge checks to identify creatures using a skill related to the subject of the book (Arcana if you’re using your spellbook). If consulting the book normally grants an item bonus to the check for consulting the book, you gain this bonus as well. If you have Shield Block, you can use a raised tome for that feat as though it were a shield. The tome has Hardness 3, HP 12, and BT 6. In addition, you can inscribe the reinforcing rune into your spellbook to strengthen your tomes, using the same process as transferring a rune. The rune takes the form of a specialized diagram in your spellbook, occupying one page. The rune’s benefits apply to any one tome in your possession chosen during your daily preparations. If your spellbook leaves your possession, the rune-granting benefit is suppressed until you get the book back.

Whenever you use an ability that allows you to Raise a Shield, such as Emergency Targe, you can Raise a Tome instead'); note mentions Hardness 3/HP 12/BT 6 and Raise-a-Shield substitution but not the reinforcing rune; actionCost passive (correct for remaster); situationalBonuses.ts raise-a-tome AC +2 circ / Recall Knowledge +1 circ (correct).

confirmed.claim: The Archives list Familiar as a 4th-level feat for the Elementalist, Shadowcaster and Soul Warden archetypes. Our record carries the single string archetype 'elementalist', which only groups or displays it; featSlots.ts slot filters admit only archetype-trait feats or the character's own class feats. So a non-magus, non-sorcerer, non-thaumaturge, non-wizard character with any of those dedications can never take Familiar, and Shadowcaster and Soul Warden are not even named.

confirmed.claim: Both of our carriers match only the plain `staff` weapon id, so a Student of the Staff magus wielding a magic staff (Staff of Fire etc., 152 weapon items with the `staff` trait, group club) gets neither the club critical specialization nor the deadly d6 in Arcane Cascade, although the feat is written about magic staves ("you can place property runes into a magic staff you prepare").

While you’re in Arcane Cascade stance, your staff gains the deadly d6 trait, with the damage from the deadly die being the same damage type as the extra damage from Arcane Cascade. In addition, you can place property runes into a magic staff you prepare, even though a magic staff can’t typically hold property runes.

confirmed.proposal: feats/student-of-the-staff critSpecWeapons -> {bases:['staff'], traits:['staff']} (effect-backfill.json); src/rules/modes.ts cat-student-of-the-staff weaponTraits -> [{match:{items:['staff']}, add:['deadly-d6']}, {match:{anyTrait:['staff']}, add:['deadly-d6']}]. Note the trait route also reaches the 3 musket staves (group firearm), which print arguably covers as 'a staff'; restrict with groups:['club'] on the mode rider if the owner prefers.
confirmed.evidence: critSpecWeapons is {bases:['staff']}, and derive.ts deriveStrike sets strike.base = w.id, so weaponMatches fails for 'staff-of-fire'. The modes.ts cat-student-of-the-staff rider tests items.includes(w.id), which also fails. items/staff-of-fire is a club-group weapon with the 'staff' trait, and 152 such items exist with no base link to 'staff'.
